probes.query: My project folder is shared by jj and plain Git. Outside jj, I use plain Git to switch to a different commit. At my next jj command, how does jj learn about that, what becomes of the commit that was my working copy, and does jj rewrite my files on disk?
expectedFacts: The CLI snapshot routine (snapshot_impl) first calls import_git_head, but only when the workspace is shared with Git, before it records the files.
git::import_head compares the Git head recorded for this workspace with the real Git HEAD and does nothing if they are equal.

CRITICAL: For a changed head, import_git_head calls MutableRepo::check_out, which writes a new working-copy commit with the new head's tree on top of the head commit and makes it the workspace's working-copy commit.
edit() abandons the old working-copy commit only if it is discardable (empty, no description), not referenced by another workspace, bookmark or tag, and is a head.
CRITICAL: Files on disk are not rewritten; the locked working copy's reset only updates the recorded tree and file states to the new commit.

DECOYS: finish_transaction/try_reset_git_head (cli_util.rs:2342,2725) go jj->Git; git::import_head_commit (git.rs:1225) imports without view update; `jj git import` (commands/git/import.rs) imports refs not HEAD. VERIFICATION: cli_util.rs:1337-1343 gate; :1382-1450 import_git_head (check_out :1401-1404, locked_wc.reset :1405-1410); git.rs:1182-1222 (equal-check :1199); repo.rs:1709-1730, :1732-1768 (is_discardable && !is_commit_referenced && heads().contains :1760-1762); local_working_copy.rs:3002-3007, :2600.

probes.query: My log shows a commit's signature as not verified even after I installed the signer's key. When does jj re-check a signature, which component decides which verifier is tried, and which results are remembered?

probes.query: When jj records my working folder, under what conditions does it re-read and re-hash a file even though its size and modification time look the same as when it last looked, and where does the reference time for that comparison come from?

probes.query: When jj compares two versions of a text in which many lines repeat, how does it choose anchor lines to line the two sides up, when does it give up on that and fall back to trimming the identical beginning and end, and what counts as a word when it refines the changed regions?

CRITICAL: The anchor search gives up immediately if even the rarest word in the left text occurs more than 100 times (max_occurrences).
It takes the lowest occurrence-count bucket of the left text that contains words with an identical occurrence count in the right text; if none exists it returns without matches.
The shared rare words are paired by position and reduced with find_lcs (longest in-order subsequence) to anchors, and the gaps between anchors are processed recursively.
For word-level refinement a word is a run of ASCII letters, digits, underscore or bytes 0x80 and above (find_word_ranges); by_word then refines changed regions with single non-word bytes.

probes.query: After a rewrite, two different jj commits could serialize to exactly the same Git commit hash while having different change IDs. How does jj stop the second from silently reusing the first one's stored metadata, where is that metadata kept, and under what condition does the retry end?
